children: Lockheed Martin Corporation (NYSE:LMT) is scaling missile and fighter production—ramping Patriot/PAC‑3 MSE and AIM‑260 output, expanding factories and suppliers, and securing big contracts and FMS sales—while supply‑chain limits and multiyear deals shape capacity, workforce and margins.
Previous Week Recap
Patriot Output Expansion Targets
: Lockheed Martin (LMT) ramps Patriot missile output: targeting ~2,000 units next year and 2,000+ annually by 2030 via factory expansion, hiring, and broader supplier base to ease supply constraints.
PAC-3 MSE Contract Expansion
: Lockheed Martin won a seven-year, up-to-$58.6B contract to supply PAC-3 MSE interceptors; U.S. aims ~2,000 missiles/year and plans to triple production capacity by 2030
AIM-260 JATM Framework
: Lockheed Martin (LMT) and DoD set a framework to speed AIM-260 JATM production and delivery, paving the way for multiyear procurement, capacity and workforce investment, and F-22/F-35 compatibility
Saudi F-35 Sale Noted
: U.S. notified Congress of a proposed $24.3B sale to Saudi Arabia including 48 Lockheed Martin F-35 jets, 49 Pratt & Whitney F135 engines, plus support, pending congressional approval.
Supply Chain Risk Highlighted
: Lockheed Martin (LMT) says supply chain is main risk to scaling production; longer subcontracts could prompt suppliers to invest in automation and capacity as multiyear demand improves planning.
First PAC-3 MSE Housings Delivered
: Lockheed Martin (LMT) received first PAC-3 MSE missile housings from GM Defense under a rapid-cycle Aug 6 contract, delivered by Aug 28 — a new second source for Patriot components.
Navy F-35 Sites Support Award
: Lockheed Martin won an $871.2M Navy award to support activation and sustainment of F-35 sites for US services and FMS. ~90% work in El Segundo, ~10% in Fort Worth; completion by Feb 2031.
Germany F-35A Deliveries Timeline
: Lockheed Martin delivered Germany’s first F-35A in Fort Worth Sept 18, 2026. Germany ordered 35 jets; 8 for training at Ebbing ANG Base this fall. Deliveries start late 2027; IOC targeted 2029.
Mission Integrator Approach
: Lockheed Martin (LMT) will act as a "mission integrator," pairing high-end weapons with lower-cost autonomous and counter-drone systems and using digital roadmaps to refresh capabilities regularly.
Low-Beta Defense Stock Backlog
: Lockheed Martin (LMT) seen as low-beta (0.3) defense stock with large missile-order backlog from Middle East conflicts; trader notes potential for steady returns and income via call-writing.
